tabs.label: Office Suite
tabs.heading: The Craft office suite
tabs.lead: WordCraft, GridCraft, PDFCraft and DeckCraft bring the open-source Craft applications to airOS. Their Rust editors run inside native Haiku windows, with system file panels, clipboard support and display scaling.
tabs.note: These are early ports of alpha applications. They render on the CPU; native printing, IME composition and some desktop integrations remain unfinished. Document compatibility varies by app. The build links below state what is currently published.

items.title: WordCraft
items.text: A word processor for longer documents, everyday writing and page layout. The Haiku port keeps the Rust editor and adds native desktop integration.
features: DOCX documents, styled text, tables, page layout and PDF export
Review tools and document recovery
Native Open/Save panels, clipboard and sharp text on scaled displays

items.title: GridCraft
items.text: A spreadsheet for budgets, calculations and charts, with a familiar ribbon and formula bar.
features: XLSX workbooks, formulas, number formats and charts
Native file panels and text/HTML clipboard integration
Tracker document handling and display-density support

items.title: PDFCraft
items.text: Read and work on PDFs in a native window, with the same Rust document engine used on the other platforms.
features: Search and copy text, annotate, edit and organize pages
Fill forms, save changes and undo edits
Native file panels, document recovery and an included command-line tool

items.title: DeckCraft
items.text: Build a presentation, add speaker notes and take it fullscreen on your Haiku desktop.
features: PPTX and DeckCraft documents, PDF and image export
Transitions, animations and a native fullscreen slide show
Media Kit audio, native file panels and recovery for unsaved work

tabs.label: Media Tools
tabs.heading: A fresh look at media
tabs.lead: Native players and a pair of Craft apps for photos: watch films in AirTime, play your music library in Amp, edit layered images in PhotoCraft and develop RAW files in LightCraft.
tabs.note: PhotoCraft and LightCraft need a hardware Vulkan driver for GPU rendering and fall back to the CPU otherwise.

items.title: AirTime
items.text: A movie player with a classic feel that plays anything FFmpeg reads, using the hardware video decoder where the machine has one.
features: Hardware decoding on AMD UVD, NVIDIA NVDEC, ROCK 5 MPP, Raspberry Pi 4 and Cubie A7S, with libavcodec as the fallback
The Movie Inspector shows which decoder is in use
HDR10 and HLG tone mapping, deinterlacing and sharp drawing on scaled displays
SRT, ASS, WebVTT, PGS, VobSub and DVB subtitles, CEA-608 captions and J/K/L scanning

items.title: Amp
items.text: A familiar music player for your local library, with Music Assistant streaming and playlists that sync back to the server.
features: MP3, AAC, FLAC, WAV and OGG libraries in song, album, grid and artist views
Stream from Music Assistant over Sendspin
Artwork lookup and MiniDisc transfers on NetMD recorders
A Quick Look add-on previews songs from Tracker with the space bar

items.title: PhotoCraft
items.text: The Craft layered image editor as a native application, drawing its canvas and interface with Vulkan.
features: Layers, brushes, masks, adjustments, 8/16/32-bit documents, PSD files and document recovery
Falls back to the CPU automatically, including when the GPU is lost mid-session
Native file panels, Tracker, clipboard and display-density support
A 24 MP opacity change measured 8–9× faster on the GPU than on the CPU

items.title: LightCraft
items.text: A photo library and RAW developer that hands photos to PhotoCraft for detailed editing.
features: Library, non-destructive developing, presets, masks and history
Vulkan compute for photo processing and a Vulkan-drawn interface, with CPU fallback
Cold previews in 65 ms instead of 455 ms on a Radeon 760M; 24 MP exports in 1.8 s instead of 4.5 s
AI models are not bundled and HEIF support is optional

tabs.label: Developer
tabs.heading: Tools for building things
tabs.lead: VS Code (Code - OSS), pgAdmin 4 and GitHub Desktop run as native airOS windows on Aurora, which reimplements Electron on Node.js with Summit’s WebKit engine and Haiku’s own menus, dialogs, clipboard and file panels. Burrow connects you to work networks.
tabs.note: VS Code (Code - OSS), pgAdmin 4 and GitHub Desktop are separate packages that have no public release yet; their port notes describe how to build them. Aurora is in x86-64 system builds. Electron features such as printing, BrowserView and screen capture are not implemented, and Linux native modules must be rebuilt for Haiku.

items.title: VS Code (Code - OSS)
items.text: Visual Studio Code’s open-source build, Code - OSS: Node.js runs the main process and Summit’s WebKit draws the windows.
features: Workbench, extension host, integrated terminal and file watching use the same code as the Linux build
Extensions come from Open VSX; Markdown previews and most extension webviews work
Native window tab and menu bar, ripgrep search and a code-oss command-line launcher
Extensions that ship Linux binaries, Copilot agent features and printing are unavailable

items.title: pgAdmin 4
items.text: pgAdmin 4 (version 9.18) in its desktop mode, with its Python server in a bundled environment.
features: Native menus, file panels, runtime settings window and quit confirmation
Query Tool tested against PostgreSQL
Uses the system’s psql, pg_dump, pg_dumpall and pg_restore (PostgreSQL 18)
Kerberos sign-in and MFA QR codes are left out

items.title: GitHub Desktop
items.text: An unofficial port of GitHub Desktop that works with Haiku’s own Git.
features: Uses the system git package and stores credentials in the Haiku key store
Browser sign-in returns to the app through its link handler
Opens Terminal, Tracker and native editors such as Pe, Koder and Genio
No usage statistics; updates come through pkgman. Git LFS is not supported

items.title: Burrow
items.text: A native client for AWS Client VPN and other OpenVPN servers, including AWS single sign-on through your web browser.
features: Import .ovpn profiles from a file panel, by drag and drop or from Tracker
SAML sign-in, certificates and username/password with challenges
Status, addresses, traffic, DNS and routes; split or full tunnel, several profiles at once
Deskbar tray menu and command-line control, with an OpenVPN built from source

tabs.label: Summit Browser
tabs.heading: Summit: the web, at home on Haiku
tabs.lead: Native controls, a compact toolbar and a modern multiprocess WebKit engine. Tabs, saved sessions, bookmarks, downloads, page find, configurable search and per-site zoom are joined by tools for reading, media, extensions and debugging.
tabs.note: Web-platform and extension compatibility are still evolving. Verified examples do not establish support for every extension or streaming service.

tabs.label: Proton
tabs.heading: Proton VPN and Proton Mail Bridge
tabs.lead: Native airOS ports of Proton’s VPN client and Mail Bridge, built from public forks. airOS CI builds each one on every push and publishes it as a rolling release with SHA-256 checksums.
tabs.note: These are unofficial community ports; they are not published or supported by Proton AG. Proton VPN is alpha: it has been tested end to end against stand-in servers and against Proton’s real sign-in API. Bridge needs a Proton plan that includes Bridge.

items.title: Proton VPN
items.text: A port of Proton’s Linux VPN app with a native Haiku interface instead of GTK. Sign in with your Proton account, pick a server and connect over WireGuard or OpenVPN.
features: Sign in with two-factor codes; the session lives in the Haiku key store
Countries, cities and Secure Core routes with loads, P2P, Tor and smart-routing badges; search, fastest-server and pinned connections in the Deskbar tray
Built-in userspace WireGuard on Haiku’s tunnel driver, or OpenVPN over UDP or TCP
NetShield, VPN Accelerator, moderate NAT, port forwarding, kill switch, custom DNS and IPv6
x86-64 and ARM64 packages, plus a proton-vpn-cli command

items.title: Proton Mail Bridge
items.text: Proton’s Bridge runs in the background and lets desktop mail apps, including airOS Mail, use your Proton Mail account over local IMAP and SMTP.
features: The upstream Go mail engine, with its vault key in the native Haiku key store; it never falls back to an unprotected vault
Proton’s Qt Quick desktop app, drawn at the desktop’s density, with a single Deskbar tray item
Native settings and data folders, start at login and a proton-bridge command
Updates come through pkgman rather than Proton’s update feed
x86-64 and ARM64 packages, also included in x86-64 system images

tabs.label: Everyday
tabs.heading: And the everyday favourites
tabs.lead: A clipboard history and a screenshot editor: small tools that are always within reach.

items.title: Clipper
items.text: A clipboard manager in the Deskbar that remembers what you copy in every app.
features: Tap Alt+V to paste; hold it, or press Shift+Alt+V, for a searchable history beside the cursor
Keeps every format: text, rich text, images and file references, with thumbnails
Pin clips, search a history of 10 to 1,000 items and pause recording
History is stored locally with owner-only permissions

items.title: AirShot
items.text: Capture a screen, window or region, mark it up, then save or copy it.
features: Full-screen, window and region captures on Print Screen shortcuts
Arrows, shapes, pen, highlighter, text, numbered markers, blur and crop, with undo
Keeps every pixel on scaled displays, with an option for 100%
Save a time-stamped PNG or copy to the clipboard; also opens existing images for markup

tabs.label: System
tabs.summary: Media preferences · MediaConverter · Bluetooth · Wi-Fi · Quick Look · Network shares · Mail · Terminal
tabs.heading: Haiku’s own apps, reworked
tabs.lead: The apps and preferences that come with the system have been rebuilt or added: clearer Media preferences, a new MediaConverter, new Wi-Fi and Bluetooth panels, Quick Look and network shares in Tracker, a new Mail app and a faster Terminal.
tabs.note: GPU encoding depends on the installed driver and card: AMD VA-API includes AV1 on verified VCN 4 hardware; NVIDIA NVENC runs a self-test before use. Other codecs and devices may use the CPU. Check MediaConverter’s Video hardware window for the current machine. Wi-Fi and Bluetooth have been tested with Intel AX210, MediaTek MT7922 and AIC8800 radios; see the hardware notes for other cards.

items.title: Media preferences
items.text: Audio and video settings have been rebuilt around a sidebar and readable cards, so devices and everyday controls are easier to find.
features: Choose input and output devices, adjust volume and play a test sound
Control individual applications in the audio mixer, with app icons and mute controls
Check a live recording level meter and camera preview
Choose a MIDI SoundFont and restart stopped media services

items.title: MediaConverter
items.text: A new conversion window and engine bring queues, previews and hardware-aware encoding to Haiku’s media toolbox.
features: Queue video and audio files, preview sources and choose separate video or audio presets
Audio conversion keeps artwork, tags and chapters, with playback controls in the source preview
Use available GPU encoders, inspect video hardware and see when a job will use the CPU
Import DVD/Blu-ray sources and disc images, sidecar subtitles and embedded closed captions
Preserve HDR10 metadata where supported; conversions run in worker processes and retry on the CPU after a GPU crash
Use the mediaconvert command-line tool for scripted conversions

items.title: Bluetooth preferences
items.text: A rebuilt Bluetooth panel for pairing mice, keyboards and audio devices, with a Bluetooth menu in the Deskbar. Adapters come up by themselves when the system starts.
features: My devices lists paired devices by kind, with Connect, Disconnect and Remove; Nearby devices finds Classic and Low Energy devices
Pair Classic and Low Energy mice and keyboards, which then reconnect automatically
Speakers and headsets can take over the system’s sound (A2DP with SBC) from the panel or the Deskbar menu; audio is still in testing
Firmware is loaded at start-up for Intel, Realtek and MediaTek USB adapters
Advanced settings for the adapter’s name, discoverability and incoming connections, plus a pairing log for diagnostics

items.title: Wi-Fi preferences
items.text: A new Wi-Fi panel shows nearby networks and joins them, with a Wi-Fi menu in the Deskbar for quick changes.
features: Turn Wi-Fi on or off and see the current network, its signal, address and whether it reaches the Internet
Known and nearby networks with signal strength and security; join with a password, remember it or forget it later
Join a hidden network by name with WEP, WPA/WPA2 Personal or WPA Enterprise
Remembered networks are joined again automatically
The Deskbar’s Wi-Fi menu lists networks and shows the channel, BSSID, PHY mode and router of the current one

items.title: Quick Look in Tracker
items.text: Press the space bar on a file in Tracker and a floating panel previews it, without opening an app.
features: Text and source code, CSV tables, pictures, PDFs, EPUBs and comic book archives
Films play with AirTime’s engine, hardware-decoded where possible; songs play with Amp’s decoder and artwork
The arrow keys move to the next file while the panel is up; several selected files are shown one at a time
The panel zooms out of the file’s icon; Open hands the file to its preferred app
Applications can add previews for their own file types through Quick Look add-ons

items.title: Network shares in Tracker
items.text: Mount folders shared by Windows, Samba and NAS servers. Tracker remembers each share and mounts it again when the system starts.
features: A Network shares page in Tracker’s preferences adds, edits, mounts and unmounts shares; Tracker’s Mount menu lists the ones not mounted
Passwords are kept in the Haiku key store; each share can mount at start-up, read-only or with SMB3 encryption
At start-up, shares are retried until the network is up, and again when the network changes; a wrong password or missing share is reported in a notification
A new smbfs file system speaks SMB2 and SMB3 and reconnects lost sessions, reopening files that were open
Kerberos, SMB1 and file attributes are not supported

items.title: Mail
items.text: A new native email client replaces Haiku’s Mail in x86-64 images. It keeps its own SQLite store and shows conversations formatted by Summit’s WebKit engine.
features: IMAP, POP3/SMTP, Gmail and Proton Mail Bridge accounts in a unified inbox; passwords and tokens stay in the Haiku key store
Conversation threads, full-text search, rules, smart folders, tags and Gmail labels
Snooze with reminders, and a rich-text composer with inline images, drafts and an Outbox
Remote content and scripts are blocked in received HTML; links open in your browser
Development release: not yet tested against live Gmail or Proton accounts, and no IMAP IDLE yet

items.title: Terminal
items.text: Haiku’s Terminal has a new emulator core and draws into one bitmap at the screen’s density, with an OpenGL renderer beside a multithreaded software renderer.
features: The GPU renderer (OpenGL 3.0) and the software renderer are timed against each other, and Terminal keeps whichever is faster
If the GPU is lost or a frame takes over two seconds, Terminal switches to software for good; force either one with the Renderer setting or TERMINAL_RENDERER
Up to 120 frames per second, a glyph atlas and Terminal-drawn box, braille and Powerline characters
Colour emoji, programming ligatures, Unicode 16 graphemes, reflow on resize and kitty protocol extensions
cat of a 5.7 MB file takes 0.14 s instead of 0.42 s; on the tested machines the software renderer is currently the faster path
